scenario: A structural engineer surveys buildings still standing after a major earthquake. Only buildings newer than 80 years old survived (older buildings were demolished or collapsed due to outdated construction standards). She records the mean age of surviving buildings to estimate the typical age of the city's building stock.

question: The surviving buildings have a mean age of 54 years. Using a truncated-from-above normal model (only buildings with age < 80 are observable), estimate (a) the true mean age Î¼ of the full pre-earthquake building stock, and (b) the fraction of buildings that survived.
naive_answer: The true mean building age is approximately 54 years since that is the observed average of surviving buildings.
naive_trap: The oldest buildings (above 80 years) were destroyed and are unobservable. For a truncated-from-above distribution, the observed mean is LOWER than the true mean. The city's building stock is actually older on average than the surviving sample suggests.

At Î¼=59.6: Î²=(80-59.6)/20=1.02, Ï†(1.02)/Î¦(1.02)=0.2347/0.8461=0.277. 59.6-20Ã—0.277=59.6-5.54=54.06 âœ“. Step 4: Fraction surviving = Î¦((80-59.6)/20)=Î¦(1.02)â‰ˆ0.846.

from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): b=(80-mu)/20; c=norm.cdf(b); return mu-20*norm.pdf(b)/c-54 if c>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,54.01,1000)
assert abs(mu-59.61)<1.0
assert abs(norm.cdf((80-mu)/20)-0.8460)<0.01
